The steam collier Brixham, which was built in Middlesbrough in 1879 and registered at 812 gross tons, arrived at Newcastle on October 12, 1884. The ship had traveled for six days from London, carrying a cargo of 640 tons of coal.

The vessel's master, Captain Elias Ward, reported that the ship lost nearly ten hours on the second day of the journey due to strong headwinds encountered off Flamborough Head. The Brixham was owned by Temperley and Carter of London, who intended for the ship to make regular coal runs between the capital and the Tyne. The ship's engines produced 900 indicated horsepower and used twenty-two tons of coal every day.

For this specific voyage, the ship was staffed by three officers and a crew of twenty-two men. Prior to departure from London, two firemen were discharged for drunkenness and were replaced by two new men who signed on only hours before the ship left the dock. The cargo was delivered in good condition, and a surveyor's certificate confirmed that there was no damage to the coamings or the hatches.

The point is situated 6 kilometres north of Praia Seca, a fishing port. A telephone line connecting the lighthouse to this port was finished in 1907. In 1912, Augusto Ferreira was succeeded as keeper by his assistant, Joao Braz, who had originally entered the service in 1898.

raw: The lighthouse at Cape Verde Point was commissioned on 3 March 1901 and was first lit by keeper Augusto Ferreira, who served there for eleven consecutive years. The tower is 34 metres high and is equipped with a second-order dioptric apparatus that shows two white flashes every fifteen seconds, visible at 18 nautical miles. The station burns kerosene at a rate of 460 litres per month, the fuel being drawn from a store built into the head keeper's cottage. A fog signal giving two blasts per minute was added in 1904 after the wreck of the barque Santa Ana, which struck the reef beneath the point on 9 July 1903 with the loss of seven hands. The point lies 6 kilometres north of the fishing port of Praia Seca, and a telephone line to that port was completed in 1907. Augusto Ferreira was succeeded in 1912 by his assistant, Joao Braz, who had joined the service in 1898.
